content: I feel so lost and worthless since they let me go. It just feels like I'm a failure, that I wasn't good enough at my job. The project I was leading got deprioritized before it even finished, and now I can't shake the feeling that it's all because of something I did wrong. Even though everyone else in my department was laid off too, I keep thinking it’s just me they didn’t want anymore. It’s like I’m being punished for not being good enough.
That must feel really tough right now. It sounds like you’re carrying a lot of self-doubt and questioning your worth. Have you had a chance to talk about these feelings with anyone?

I’ve tried talking to friends, but it’s hard because they just tell me I’m overthinking things or that the layoff was nothing personal. It doesn’t really help though; deep down, I still feel like this is all my fault. My manager didn’t even give me much of a chance to explain myself during our meeting—it felt so dismissive and made me feel like they never thought highly of me in the first place.

I know logically that it was just restructuring, but I can't seem to shake these feelings of being inadequate or not measuring up. It’s exhausting trying to convince myself otherwise.

It sounds really tough how your manager's reaction added to those feelings. Have you thought about reaching out to a counselor or someone who might be able to listen more deeply and help you work through some of these thoughts? Sometimes talking to someone who can offer a different perspective can be helpful.

That’s such a kind suggestion, thank you for thinking of that. I’ve been considering it but feel so stuck in this mindset that even reaching out feels like admitting defeat. It’s hard to imagine anyone could really help me see things differently when I’m convinced these feelings are true.

But maybe talking to someone who isn’t as close to the situation could provide some clarity or at least make me feel less alone with all of this. I just worry it won’t change how I truly feel about myself and my worth.

It’s really brave that you’re considering reaching out, even if it feels daunting right now. Sometimes talking things through can help shift your perspective a bit. Even if the feelings don’t disappear completely, having someone else’s view might make them feel a little lighter. Would you like to explore this further or do you have another idea in mind for how to move forward?

You’re so understanding and supportive, thank you. It does sound daunting, but maybe it could be the first step toward feeling better about myself again. I just hope that talking won’t make me feel worse or confirm my fears even more.

I’m not sure what else to do right now besides keep trying to find a new job, but every rejection letter feels like another confirmation of my worthlessness. It’s overwhelming and exhausting, and I don’t know how much longer I can push through this on my own.

It sounds like you’re doing a lot already by keeping at it with your job search. Talking to someone could indeed be a helpful step without adding too much pressure. Maybe starting small, like just one session or call, could give you an idea of how it feels and if it helps. How do you feel about giving it a try?

That sounds manageable, at least trying out one session. It’s comforting to think that I don’t have to commit fully right away. Maybe talking to someone will help me see things from a different angle or give me some tools to handle these feelings better.

I’m just so worried about failing again though—what if this doesn’t work either? It feels like every attempt I make ends up proving how incapable I am. But maybe taking that first step could be the start of something positive.

It’s a brave step you’re considering, and it makes sense to feel nervous about trying something new. Taking that first step can often lead to some relief or new insights. Even if it doesn’t work out as expected, just knowing you tried can be empowering. Would you like to start by looking for someone nearby or online?

You’re so supportive and understanding. I think starting with one session sounds doable, maybe even finding someone online since that feels less intimidating right now. It’s comforting to know that taking this step could help me see things differently.

I’m still scared about failing again though—I feel like every time I try something new, it ends up showing how much I can’t handle or how little value I have. But maybe giving therapy a chance is worth the risk of feeling even more vulnerable for now.

It’s really brave to consider taking that first step, especially given your concerns about vulnerability. Starting with an online session might indeed feel less daunting. You’re right; it’s worth considering how this could help you see things differently and provide some relief. How does the idea of finding a therapist online sound to you? Would you like some suggestions on where to start?

Finding a therapist online sounds more manageable, thank you for suggesting that. I appreciate your support—it means a lot to know someone believes this could be helpful.

I’m still nervous about it all, but maybe starting with just one session can help me see if talking to someone really does make a difference. It’s comforting to think there might be some relief or clarity on the other side of that first step.

That sounds like a great plan. Taking it one step at a time can definitely make it feel more manageable. I’m glad you’re considering giving it a try, and I hope it brings you some relief and clarity. How about we start by looking for some online therapists together? Do you have any preferences or specific things you’d like to focus on in therapy?

That sounds good to me, thank you. Looking for an online therapist feels less overwhelming than finding someone locally right now. I don’t have specific preferences yet, but maybe focusing on helping me feel better about myself and my worth would be a good start.

I’m just worried it will all fall apart again—what if talking doesn’t help or makes things worse? But you’re right; starting with one session could give me some clarity. Let’s see what options are out there and take it from there.

It’s a great idea to focus on building self-worth and confidence. Starting with one session will definitely give you a sense of whether it feels helpful.
